en.caution: Do not confuse a single 14.45% headline-driven bounce with a confirmed bottom. LRCX opened at $217.17 on November 23 and faded to $209.76, proving sellers are still defending the $221.13 Bollinger middle band and heavy moving-average resistance above $253. Meanwhile, China jumped to 35% of Q1 FY2027 revenue, leaving earnings vulnerable to tighter U.S. export rules or Chinese rare-earth curbs. Ongoing congressional scrutiny around Nvidia and industry cleanroom constraints persisting into 2027 could trigger renewed volatility.
cons: Despite the November 23 bounce to $209.76, shares remain 52.2% below their $438.50 52-week high and in a bearish technical structure below all major EMAs.
China surged back to 35% of Q1 FY2027 revenue (up from 26% in the June quarter), keeping Lam highly exposed to U.S.–China export controls and rare-earth restrictions.
Management warned on October 21 that supply-chain and cleanroom bottlenecks capped December-quarter upside and will likely persist through 2027.
Several Wall Street banks trimmed 12-month price targets after earnings (including Citi, UBS, Morgan Stanley on October 22 and B. Riley on November 9), reflecting compressed sector multiples.
en.fundamental: Lam Research's etch and deposition leadership is directly monetizing AI infrastructure buildouts. In Q1 FY2027 (ended September 27, 2026), revenue jumped 54% YoY and 22% sequentially to a record $8.22 billion—$5.73 billion from systems and $2.49 billion from recurring Customer Support Business Group (CSBG) services. End-market shipments split evenly between foundry (46%) and memory (46%), with logic/IDM at 8%, as HBM stacking, DRAM scaling, and panel-level packaging lifted memory systems revenue roughly 120% YoY. Non-GAAP gross margin hit a multi-year high of 52.4%, operating margin reached 40.2%, and EPS came in at $2.20. For the December 2026 quarter, management guided revenue to $8.60 billion (±$400 million) and EPS to $2.33 (±$0.15), while forecasting over $200 billion in calendar 2027 industry WFE spending with customer visibility into 2028.

news: November 23, 2026: LRCX surged 14.45% to $209.76 after Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated CEO Jensen Huang—11 days after his November 12 resignation sparked a sector-wide AI-hardware selloff that pushed LRCX down 10.02% to $183.27 on November 20 alongside double-digit drops in peers Applied Materials and KLA.

November 23, 2026: Lam partnered with the University at Albany's College of Nanotechnology, Science, and Engineering to integrate its Semiverse Solutions and SEMulator3D virtual-fabrication software into engineering curricula.

November 5, 2026: Lam's board authorized a $25 billion share repurchase program with no expiration date (supplementing prior remaining capacity) and declared a $0.33 quarterly dividend payable January 6, 2027 to shareholders of record on December 2, 2026.

October 22–November 9, 2026: Following earnings and sector multiple compression, Citi ($450 to $435), UBS ($425 to $400), and Morgan Stanley ($385 to $339) cut 12-month price targets on October 22 while maintaining Buy/Overweight ratings; B. Riley followed on November 9, trimming its target from $338 to $310 with a Buy rating.

October 21–22, 2026: Lam reported record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $8.22 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $2.20, guiding Q2 FY2027 revenue to $8.60 billion while its October 22 Form 10-Q flagged export-control, rare-earth licensing, and supply-chain risks.
en.opportunity: The stark disconnect between a 52.2% stock drawdown from $438.50 and record operational execution creates an interesting setup for patient long-term investors watching for technical stabilization. Lam's etch and deposition moat is strengthening as HBM stacking, advanced-node logic, and panel-level packaging push industry WFE toward an expected $200 billion-plus in 2027. Backed by $7.45 billion in cash, $2.66 billion in deferred revenue, and a $25 billion buyback authorization, Lam can retire substantial shares if prices stay depressed near $183–$210.
en.opportunityCheck: The page's strong score for market position fits Lam's leadership in HBM, DRAM, and advanced-node etch and deposition, while market growth and optionality look appropriately balanced for a cyclical equipment maker. However, AI revenue exposure looks too conservative and warrants an upward revision: Q1 FY2027 revenue jumped 54% YoY to $8.22 billion, memory systems surged 120% YoY, and panel-level AI packaging tools now serve over 20 customers. Bottleneck and pricing power could also move modestly higher given record 52.4% gross margins and industry cleanroom constraints persisting through 2027.
pros: Record Q1 FY2027 revenue jumped 54% YoY to $8.22 billion on October 21, 2026, with memory systems soaring 120% YoY on HBM and DRAM spending.
Non-GAAP gross margin reached a multi-year high of 52.4% and operating margin hit 40.2%, with Q2 FY2027 revenue guided higher to $8.60 billion.
On November 5, 2026, the board approved a massive $25 billion share repurchase program alongside a $0.33 quarterly dividend, backed by $7.45 billion in cash.
Management projected calendar 2027 wafer-fabrication equipment (WFE) spending above $200 billion and shipped panel-level AI packaging tools to over 20 customers.
risks: Geopolitical and export-control risk: China represented 35% of Q1 FY2027 revenue, and Lam's October 22 Form 10-Q flagged both U.S. licensing curbs and Chinese rare-earth export restrictions.
AI capex cyclicality: Skepticism over hyperscaler returns on AI data-center spending or renewed governance turbulence at key ecosystem bellwethers like Nvidia can compress WFE multiples rapidly.
Supply-chain and cleanroom bottlenecks: CFO Doug Bettinger warned on October 21 that component and customer cleanroom constraints capped December-quarter upside and will persist through 2027.
Technical breakdown risk: With EMA 50 below EMA 200 and price stuck beneath the $221.13 Bollinger midline, a break below $182.89 would expose LRCX to deeper downside toward the $135.50 52-week low.
en.summary: Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) rallied 14.45% to $209.76 on November 23, 2026 after Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang, snapping a brutal AI-chip selloff that dragged LRCX down 10.02% to $183.27 on November 20. Fundamentally, the moat remains intact: Q1 FY2027 revenue hit a record $8.22 billion (+54% YoY) with 52.4% non-GAAP gross margin and a new $25 billion buyback announced November 5. Technically, however, LRCX sits 52.2% below its $438.50 52-week high and far under all key moving averages, leaving the trend bearish.
en.technical: As of November 23, 2026, LRCX remains in a bearish trend despite surging 14.45% to $209.76. Price sits 17% to 23% below its exponential moving averages (EMAs, which smooth price to show trend): EMA 50 ($253.34), EMA 200 ($264.17), and EMA 100 ($272.44). Because EMA 50 has crossed below EMA 200—a bearish "death cross"—the multi-month structure is damaged. Momentum shows early stabilization rather than reversal: RSI 14 (a 0–100 momentum gauge where under 30 is oversold) recovered to 42.32, still below the neutral 50 mark, while MACD (a trend-momentum oscillator) remains deeply negative at -17.64 but edged above its -18.11 signal line for a +0.47 histogram. Within Bollinger Bands (a 20-day volatility channel spanning $182.89 to $259.38), LRCX bounced off the lower band but failed to reclaim the $221.13 middle line, fading from its $217.19 intraday high. Trading in the bottom quarter of its $135.50–$438.50 52-week range, Monday's 17.25 million share volume (23.5% above the 13.97 million 20-day average) confirmed strong participation alongside overhead selling. Key support sits at $204.65 and $182.89; resistance stands at $217.19–$221.13 and $253.34.

th.summary: Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) พุ่งขึ้น 14.45% ปิดที่ $209.76 เมื่อวันที่ 23 พ.ย. 2026 หลัง Nvidia คืนตำแหน่งซีอีโอให้ Jensen Huang ช่วยคลายแรงเทขายหุ้นชิป AI ที่เพิ่งฉุด LRCX ร่วง 10.02% เหลือ $183.27 เมื่อ 20 พ.ย. ในเชิงพื้นฐานคูเมืองธุรกิจยังแข็งแกร่ง โดยรายได้ Q1 FY2027 ทำสถิติใหม่ที่ $8.22 พันล้าน (+54% YoY) อัตรากำไรขั้นต้น Non-GAAP แตะ 52.4% พร้อมประกาศซื้อหุ้นคืน $25 พันล้านเมื่อ 5 พ.ย. แต่ทางเทคนิคราคายังต่ำกว่าจุดสูงสุดรอบ 52 สัปดาห์ที่ $438.50 ถึง 52.2% และอยู่ใต้เส้นค่าเฉลี่ยหลักทั้งหมด แนวโน้มจึงยังเป็นขาลง
th.technical: ณ วันที่ 23 พ.ย. 2026 โครงสร้างทางเทคนิคของ LRCX ยังคงเป็นขาลงแม้จะดีดกลับ 14.45% มาที่ $209.76 โดยราคาอยู่ต่ำกว่าเส้นค่าเฉลี่ยเคลื่อนที่เอ็กซ์โปเนนเชียล (EMA ซึ่งใช้กรองแนวโน้มราคา) ทุกเส้นราว 17%–23% ได้แก่ EMA 50 ($253.34), EMA 200 ($264.17) และ EMA 100 ($272.44) การที่ EMA 50 ตัดลงต่ำกว่า EMA 200 (สัญญาณ Death Cross) บ่งชี้ว่าแนวโน้มหลายเดือนยังเสียหาย ด้านโมเมนตัมเริ่มเห็นสัญญาณชะลอแรงลงแต่ยังไม่กลับตัว โดย RSI 14 (มาตรวัดแรงเหวี่ยงระดับ 0–100 ต่ำกว่า 30 คือขายมากเกินไป) ฟื้นมาอยู่ที่ 42.32 ยังต่ำกว่าระดับกลาง 50 ขณะที่ MACD (เครื่องมือวัดแรงส่งของแนวโน้ม) ยังติดลบหนักที่ -17.64 แต่ขยับเหนือเส้น Signal ที่ -18.11 จนได้ค่า Histogram +0.47 ในกรอบ Bollinger Bands (ช่องความผันผวน 20 วัน ระหว่าง $182.89–$259.38) หุ้นดีดจากขอบล่างแต่ยังไม่ผ่านเส้นกลางที่ $221.13 หลังอ่อนตัวลงจากจุดสูงสุดระหว่างวันที่ $217.19 ราคาปัจจุบันอยู่ช่วงล่างสุด 25% ของกรอบ 52 สัปดาห์ ($135.50–$438.50) ขณะที่วอลุ่มวันจันทร์อยู่ที่ 17.25 ล้านหุ้น สูงกว่าค่าเฉลี่ย 20 วัน (13.97 ล้านหุ้น) ถึง 23.5% ยืนยันแรงซื้อกลับพร้อมแรงขายทำกำไร แนวรับสำคัญอยู่ที่ $204.65 และ $182.89 ส่วนแนวต้านอยู่ที่ $217.19–$221.13 และ $253.34
